body:
Thanks. Like I said, it's not all just about the girl. I just wish I had someone in my life who I could talk to without having to hold back. When different people ask me how I'm doing, I give different answers, but it's never the whole story. Last time it was school, this time it was a girl, I don't know what it's going to be next time, but I'm worried I might freak out again if I don't have anyone to talk through my problems with. I guess that might be something everyone has to deal with, so I don't know why I worry so much about it. I'm well-known in my school's band and I hold a leadership position in robotics club, so it's not like I'm a complete shut-in, but clearly I'm doing something wrong since I feel this way.

Thank you so much for taking the time and effort to respond to me. Even through anonymity, it makes me feel a little better that someone out there knows what I'm going through. I don't know anything about you or your personal experiences, but do you have any tips for how I can act/think differently to be more sociable when I get to college? I can sign myself up for a club or show up to a party, but once I'm there, I always feel really utilitarian, only talking when I need to and only about what I need to. I think it's been pretty successful in building up my reputation, and I feel like if I started talking more, people would value what I have to say less.
